lines.text: Empty islands in the Atlantic, settled by the Portuguese, scarred by slavery, and set to music by their people. This is Cape Verde.
In 1462 the Portuguese founded Cidade Velha on Santiago, the first European colonial town in the tropics.
Later, Praia grew on the same island. It is the capital today.
Out of hard island lives came morna, a slow, sad song now honoured by UNESCO as part of the world's heritage.
Aristides Pereira, born in 1923, would become the first president of a free Cape Verde.
Amilcar Cabral, born in 1924, would lead the fight against Portuguese rule here and in Guinea-Bissau.
Pedro Pires, born in 1934, would later serve as president and win the Mo Ibrahim Prize for good leadership.
In 1936, Portugal opened a prison camp at Tarrafal on Santiago, for those who opposed its rule.
Cesaria Evora was born in 1941. The barefoot diva would carry the islands' songs to the whole world.
In 1956 Cabral helped found the PAIGC, the party that would fight for the freedom of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde.
Ulisses Correia e Silva, born in 1962, has been prime minister since 2016.
Cabral was killed in 1973, but two years later, in 1975, Cape Verde was independent.
Small islands with a great voice, Cape Verde sings its story to the world.
